title: Russia completes the withdrawal of its peacekeeping contingent from Nagorno-Karabakh
body:
Azerbaijan's Defense Ministry said on 12 June 2024 that the withdrawal of the Russian peacekeeping contingent from Nagorno-Karabakh had concluded. The ministry stated that the personnel, weapons and equipment of the peacekeeping contingent had completely left Azerbaijani territory. The Kyiv Independent reported the statement the same day. Russia had deployed several thousand peacekeepers to the region in autumn 2020 after the Moscow-brokered ceasefire that ended the second Nagorno-Karabakh war.

The withdrawal began in April 2024, several months after Azerbaijan captured the region in a military offensive in September 2023. That offensive ended in less than 24 hours with Azerbaijan's victory and the dissolution of the self-declared Nagorno-Karabakh Republic. After the region's surrender, around 100,000 Armenians, the majority of the population, left for Armenia.

The pullout came amid worsening Armenian-Russian relations. In March 2024 Armenia asked Russian peacekeepers stationed at Yerevan's international airport to leave. In February, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan had said Armenia had frozen its participation in the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization, which he said had failed to uphold its objectives regarding Armenia. Armenia was also considering applying for European Union membership.
